---
title: "Comparing Total MEs across models"
subtitle: "Example 5.2.e of Mize and Han (2025): mediation/attenuation with a multi-category outcome"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

With a nominal or ordinal outcome, each predictor has one marginal effect per
outcome category, so a cross-model comparison of "the" effect of a predictor
means comparing several effects at once. The Total ME of Mize and Han (2025)
sums the absolute effects across the outcome categories (and halves the sum)
to give one number: the total probability mass the predictor moves. The
`totalme` option of `mecompare` adds that summary above the per-category
effects, and with two models in `models()` the **Difference** row tests
whether the Total ME changed.

Here the question is whether the total effect of a college degree on
self-rated health shrinks once family income is in the model. The outcome
has five ordered categories and is fit with a multinomial logit on the
2000--2021 GSS. Store the model without income and the model with it, and
name both in `models()`; the models are combined with
[`suest2`](../../suest2/index.html) so that the test of the difference
accounts for the two models being estimated on the same data.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss", clear
drop if missing(healthR, college, race4, age, woman, parent, married, faminc)
drop if year < 2000 | year > 2021

quietly mlogit healthR i.college i.race4 c.age i.woman i.parent i.married, vce(robust)
estimates store basemod

quietly mlogit healthR i.college i.race4 c.age i.woman i.parent i.married c.faminc, vce(robust)
estimates store medmod
<</dd_do>>
```

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare i.college, models(basemod medmod) totalme
<</dd_do>>
```

The first block of the table is the Total ME of a college degree in each
model and its **Difference**: the part of the total college effect that
family income accounts for, with a standard error and p-value. The blocks
beneath it are the marginal effects of college on each health category,
each with its own cross-model difference, so the table shows both the
summary and which categories the attenuation comes from. As on every
`mecompare` table the rows are numbered, so
[`metest`](../../metest/index.html) can express the attenuation as a
proportion of the baseline Total ME:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest (1 - 2) / 1
<</dd_do>>
```

The same difference is what `totalme college, models(basemod medmod)`
reports; `mecompare` adds the per-category effects and the row numbers for
`metest`. `totalme` works the same way for continuous predictors (with
`amount()` setting the size of the change) and, for nominal predictors,
reports a Total ME inequality; the
[Options](../options.html#meinequality-and-totalme-summary-measures) page
has an example of each.

## Reference

> Mize, Trenton D. and Bing Han. 2025. "Inequality and Total Effect Summary
> Measures for Nominal and Ordinal Variables." *Sociological Science* 12:
> 115--157.
